name: PoWER-BERT
main_result: BERT-base (SST-2): acc 92.1 at 374 ms per batch of 128 on K80 (baseline 93.0 at 905 ms), 2.4x
notes: Score = total attention a word-vector receives (column sum over heads), not only CLS. Retention configuration (count per layer, same for all inputs) learned by soft-extract layers with an L1 mass regularizer. Three steps: fine-tune, configuration search, re-train. Inference time on K80 with batch 128.
evidence: "the significance score is the total amount of attention imposed by w on the other words" (Sec. 3.2); "we design a strategy that learns the retention configuration" (Sec. 3.3); "Given a dataset, the scheme involves three training steps: 1. Fine-tuning ... 2. Configuration-search ... 3. Re-training" (Sec. 3.4)

name: Funnel-Transformer
main_result: B6-6-6H768 vs L12H768: GLUE-avg 85.3 at 0.88x FLOPs (baseline 84.4 at 1.00x)
notes: Strided mean pooling (window 2, stride 2) halves the sequence between blocks; pooled sequence is used only as query (pool-query-only). Decoder up-samples for token-level tasks. Pre-trained from scratch (MLM or ELECTRA) then fine-tuned. Running time on V100 GPU and TPU v2-8 in Appendix C.2 with batch sizes 4-64 per device.
evidence: "we find the simplest strided mean pooling applied to each sliding window of the sequence work very well in practice" (Sec. 2.2); "we empirically evaluate the proposed F-TFM by first pretraining it and then finetuning it in downstream tasks" (Sec. 4)

name: TR-BERT
main_result: BERT-base (SQuAD 2.0): F1 75.66 at 2.08x FLOPs speedup (baseline 77.12)
notes: Policy network (2-layer FFN) trained by REINFORCE with imitation warm-up, then whole network fine-tuned; two reduction modules (before layers 2 and 6). Skipped tokens keep their last representation for prediction. Count varies per input; the inference-time decision rule is not stated, so schedule is set to other. Wall time: 2.08x FLOPs gives 2.01x on V100 with batch 32.
evidence: "TR-BERT employs the reinforcement learning (RL) method to learn the dynamic token selection strategy automatically" (Sec. 1); "(3) Unfreeze all parameters and train the entire network with the task-specific objective and RL objective simultaneously" (Sec. 3.2)

name: Length-Adaptive Transformer
main_result: BERT-base (SQuAD 1.1): F1 88.7 at 0.45x FLOPs (baseline 88.5 at 1.00x)
notes: Uses the PoWER-BERT significance score. LengthDrop trains one model for any length configuration; an evolutionary search picks the configuration for a given FLOPs budget without re-training. Drop-and-Restore keeps dropped vectors aside and restores them at the last layer for token-level tasks. Fig. 3 reports latency vs FLOPs on GPU and CPU at batch 1, 4, 16, 64.
evidence: "We train a transformer with LengthDrop, a structural variant of dropout, which stochastically determines a sequence length at each layer. We then conduct a multi-objective evolutionary search to find a length configuration that maximizes the accuracy and minimizes the efficiency metric under any given computational budget" (Abstract); "Drop-and-Restore, does not eliminate word vectors at each layer according to the length configuration but instead sets them aside until the final hidden layer" (Sec. 3.3)

name: LTP
main_result: RoBERTa-base (QQP): acc 89.69 at 2.53 GFLOPs (baseline 90.39 at 5.31), 2.10x
notes: Score = column mean of attention probability averaged over heads (attention received from all tokens). Per-layer thresholds learned with a soft sigmoid mask and an L1 regularizer; then mask binarized and model fine-tuned. Throughput up to 1.9x on V100 and 2.0x on Intel Haswell CPU (Fig. 6, several batch sizes; the batch sizes are not given in the text, so batch1 is unknown).
evidence: "LTP prunes tokens with an attention score below a threshold, whose value is learned for each layer during training" (Abstract); "After (i) jointly training model parameters and thresholds on downstream tasks with the soft pruning scheme, (ii) we fix the thresholds and binarize the soft mask, and (iii) perform a follow-up fine-tuning of the model parameters" (Sec. 3.3)

name: DynamicViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.3 at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Keep ratio 0.7 per stage before blocks 4, 7, 10 (0.7, 0.49, 0.34 of tokens). MLP predictor with local and global features; Gumbel-softmax and attention masking in training. 30 epochs from the pretrained model, backbone LR 0.01x, backbone frozen for the first 5 epochs; KL and token distillation from the unpruned model. Throughput on one RTX 3090 with batch 32.
evidence: "we devise a lightweight prediction module to estimate the importance score of each token given the current features" (Abstract); "During inference, we only need to select the most informative tokens according to a predefined pruning ratio and the scores computed by the prediction modules" (Sec. 3.1); "We use the pre-trained vision transformer models to initialize the backbone models and jointly train the whole model for 30 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: DynamicViT / DynamicCNN / DynamicSwin
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; ConvNeXt-T/S/B; Swin-T/S/B
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.3 at 3.0 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Journal extension of DynamicViT (same predictor and ratio schedule). For hierarchical models the uninformative locations are not dropped but sent through a lightweight linear fast path instead of the FFN (asymmetric computation), which keeps the feature-map structure; that is the other part of operation. Dense tasks (ADE20k, COCO) use DynamicCNN on ConvNeXt, not DeiT. DeiT-S trained 30 epochs from pretrained; DynamicCNN 120 epochs. Throughput on one RTX 3090 with batch 128 (numbers differ slightly from the NeurIPS version).
evidence: "By applying lightweight fast paths to less informative features and expressive slow paths to important locations, we can maintain the complete structure of feature maps while significantly reducing the overall computations" (Abstract); "The training process includes training the prediction modules such that they can produce favorable decisions and fine-tuning the backbone to make it adapt to spatial sparsification" (Sec. 3.3)

name: IA-RED2
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.1 at >=1360 fps (baseline 79.8 at <=930 fps, V100)
notes: Multi-head interpreter (policy token dot product with patch tokens, sigmoid) before each of 3 groups of 4 blocks; a patch is dropped if its score is below 0.5, so the count varies per image. Interpreters trained by REINFORCE with an efficiency reward, then the MSA-FFN blocks are fine-tuned, in a curriculum over groups (3 x 30 epochs). Main table gives only fps bounds (>=1360 for IA-RED2, <=930 for DeiT-S; V100-32GB, PyTorch 1.7, batch size not stated), so 1360/930 = 1.46x is a lower bound of the speed-up. GFLOPs for DeiT-S appears only in Appendix D (79.1% at 2.9 G); Table 8 lists 79.1% at 3.4 G for tau=1.5 and SViT Table 7 quotes 3.2 G, so the number is uncertain. Code URL is the project page; no repository link in the paper.
evidence: "adopt a policy network (referred to as multi-head interpreter) to decide which patches are uninformative and then discard them" (Sec. 1); "If Iij is below the threshold 0.5, the patch Xi will be completely discarded at j th group and will not be available in the subsequent groups" (Sec. 3.2); "We optimize the multi-head interpreters by using the REINFORCE method where the reward considers both the efficiency and accuracy, and finetune the MSA-FFN blocks with gradients computed based on cross-entropy loss" (Sec. 3.2)

name: SViTE+
main_result: DeiT-S (SViTE+, 50% unstructured weight sparsity, 95% tokens): top-1 80.18 at 49.32% FLOPs saving (baseline 79.90)
notes: Main contribution is dynamic sparse training of weights (prune-and-grow); SViTE+ adds a learnable token selector (MLP scorer + top-k with Gumbel-softmax straight-through) that drops 5-10% of input tokens. Trained from scratch for 600 epochs. FLOPs given only as % saving, so GFLOPs is unknown. Running time reported as % reduction per iteration in CUDA benchmark mode (4.40% at 95% tokens), device not stated.
evidence: "plugging in a novel learnable token selector to adaptively determine the currently most vital patches" (Abstract); "Then, a selection of the top-k importance scores (1 ≤ k ≤ d) is applied on top of it, aiming to preserve the significant tokens and remove the useless ones" (Sec. 3.2); "we increase training epochs to 600 for all experiments" (Sec. 4)

name: DGE
main_result: PVT-S: top-1 80.2 at 3.5 GFLOPs (baseline 80.2 at 6.2)
notes: Each S x S region gets a granularity (1, 2 or 4) from a gating network; patches are average pooled into queries, keys/values stay dense, output is un-pooled to full resolution with a residual. Budget loss with target ratio gamma=0.5 during training; per-image count varies. All models re-trained 300 epochs at 256x256. DeiT-S+DGE appears only in Fig. 5 (no number in text). Latency on Xeon 6130 CPU and V100 GPU for one 800x1280 (COCO) or 512x2048 (ADE20k) image.
evidence: "For each region, the number of patches is decided by a data-dependent routing process, and each patch is average pooled to obtain a 1D token" (Sec. 1); "we define a computational budget denoted as γ ∈ [0, 1], which corresponds to the desired computational complexity ratio relative to the vanilla encoder without dynamic grained" (Sec. 3.2.3); "All the models are trained for 300 epochs with 128 images per batch" (Sec. 4.1.1)

name: DVT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.4 at 2.90 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.61)
notes: Cascade of transformers with 7x7, 10x10, 14x14 tokens; exit when the max softmax probability reaches a threshold; thresholds solved by a genetic algorithm for a FLOPs budget. Feature and relationship reuse between stages. Criterion is prediction confidence, not a token score. Trained with the backbone recipe (initialization from pretrained weights not mentioned). Throughput only for T2T-ViT on a 2080Ti with batch 128.
evidence: "This is achieved by cascading multiple Transformers with increasing numbers of tokens, which are sequentially activated in an adaptive fashion at test time, i.e., the inference is terminated once a sufficiently confident prediction is produced" (Abstract); "we simply train DVT to produce correct predictions at all exits" (Sec. 3.1); "The training of DVT follows exactly the same configurations as the backbones" (Appendix A)

name: TokenLearner
backbones: ViT-S/32; ViT-B/32; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; ViT-L/14; ViT-L/10; ViT-L/8; ViViT
main_result: ViT-B/16 (JFT-300M pretrain, 384px): top-1 83.65 at 28.7 GFLOPs (baseline 84.73 at 55.6)
notes: 8 or 16 tokens generated by S spatial attention maps (conv or MLP) applied to the input and spatially pooled; inserted at the middle of the network (or later); TokenFuser maps back to the original shape. Pre-trained on JFT-300M with TokenLearner inserted, then fine-tuned on ImageNet, so numbers are not comparable with DeiT. Runtime: ViT-L/16 1400 vs 2000 images/s with TokenLearner (device not stated).
evidence: "TokenLearner is a learnable module that takes an image-like tensor (i.e., input) and generates a small set of tokens" (Sec. 1); "We compute spatial attention maps highlighting regions-of-importance (using convolutional layers or MLPs), and they are applied to the input itself to weight each region differently (and discard unnecessary regions). The results are spatially pooled to generate the final learned tokens" (Sec. 1); "we pre-train the model with JFT and fine-tune it with the original ImageNet dataset" (Sec. 3.4)

name: EViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.5 at 3.0 GMACs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Keep rate 0.7 at layers 4, 7, 10; CLS attention averaged over heads; inattentive tokens fused into one token by attention-weighted average. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs (keep rate warmed up with a cosine schedule); also fine-tunes from a pretrained DeiT with an oracle (Table 6) and at higher resolution. Cost is reported as MACs (torchprofile), entered in the GFLOPs column. Throughput on one A100 with batch 128.
evidence: "we identify the attentive image tokens between MHSA and FFN (i.e., feed-forward network) modules, which is guided by the corresponding class token attention. Then, we reorganize image tokens by preserving attentive image tokens and fusing inattentive ones" (Abstract); "We train the models with EViT from scratch for 300 epochs on 16 NVIDIA A100 GPUs" (Sec. 4)

name: Evo-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 1510 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 940 img/s, V100 batch 256)
notes: Global class attention (residual over layers) selects top-k (ratio 0.5) from layer 5. Placeholder tokens are summed into one representative token that goes through MSA/FFN with the informative tokens; the placeholder tokens are kept and fast-updated by copying the representative token's residual, so the 2D structure is preserved (halt part). 300 epochs from scratch with a layer-to-stage schedule. No FLOPs reported, only throughput.
evidence: "we conduct unstructured instance-wise token selection by taking advantage of the simple and effective global class attention that is native to vision transformers" (Abstract); "the placeholder tokens are summarized to a representative token that is evolved via the full transformer encoder simultaneously with the informative tokens in a slow and elaborate way. Then, the evolved representative token is exploited to fast update the placeholder tokens" (Sec. 1); "For fair comparisons, all the models are trained for 300 epochs" (Experiments, Setup)

name: A-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 78.6 at 3.6 GFLOPs (baseline 78.9 at 4.6, DeiT-S fine-tuned without distillation)
notes: Halting score = sigmoid of one embedding dimension of each token (no extra parameters); a token is removed once its cumulative score reaches 1-eps; ponder loss plus a distributional prior on the exit depth. 100 epochs fine-tuning from pretrained DeiT without mixup or distillation token (with distillation token: 80.7). Throughput given as 1.1K imgs/s on an RTX 2080 with batch 64. Code URL is the project page.
evidence: "A token is discarded once reaching the halting condition" (Fig. 1 caption); "we conduct the token stopping when the cumulative halting score exceeds 1 − ε" (Sec. 3); "Starting from publicly available pretrained checkpoints, we fine-tune DeiT-T/S variant models for 100 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: AdaViT
main_result: T2T-ViT-19: top-1 81.1 at 3.9 GFLOPs (baseline 81.9 at 8.5)
notes: A decision network before each block predicts keep/drop for patches, attention heads and the MSA/FFN sub-layers; Gumbel-softmax in training with a usage loss toward budgets gamma_p, gamma_h, gamma_b; binary decisions by thresholding at inference, so the count varies per image. Backbone initialized from pretrained T2T-ViT and trained 150 epochs. Only FLOPs reported. Paper says the code will be released; no URL.
evidence: "a light-weight decision network is attached to the backbone to produce decisions on-the-fly" (Abstract); "As the decisions are binary, the action of keeping / discarding can be selected by simply applying a threshold on the entries during inference" (Sec. 3.2); "We initialize the transformer backbone of AdaViT with the pretrained weights released in the official implementation of [50]" (Sec. 4.1)

name: PS-ViT (Patch Slimming)
backbones: DeiT-Ti; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; T2T-ViT-14; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.6 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Top-down: patches kept in layer l+1 are also kept in layer l. Impact score of a patch = effect on the last-layer reconstruction error, computed from products of attention maps of the deeper layers (Theorem 1) and averaged over a data subset, so the mask is static (same for all images). Count per layer set by a tolerant error eps. Each block is fine-tuned for 3 epochs after selection, then the whole model is fine-tuned. Dynamic variant DPS-ViT adds a small predictor per block (79.5 at 2.4 G). Throughput device and batch size not stated (experiments on V100). No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "We first identify the effective patches in the last layer and then use them to guide the patch selection process of previous layers. For each layer, the impact of a patch on the final output feature is approximated and patches with less impact will be removed" (Abstract); "After pruning, the mask ml is fixed, and weight parameters in the vision transformer is further fine-tuned to be compatible with the efficient architecture" (Sec. 4.3)

name: ATS
backbones: DeiT-S; CvT-13; CvT-21; PS-ViT-B/14; PS-ViT-B/18; XViT; TimeSformer
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.7 at 2.9 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6), after 30-epoch fine-tuning
notes: Score = CLS attention weight times ||V_j||, summed over heads; parameter-free. Tokens chosen by inverse transform sampling over the score CDF with at most K samples; duplicates removed, so the count K' varies per image (schedule set to other because there is no threshold). Training-free use on a pretrained DeiT-S: about 0.6% drop (Appendix C); fine-tuned variant: 30 epochs following the DynamicViT setup. Multi-stage: ATS in blocks 3-11. Throughput on an RTX 6000 (batch size not stated). Code URL is the project page.
evidence: "Since ATS is a parameter-free module, it can be added to the off-the-shelf pre-trained vision transformers as a plug and play module, thus reducing their GFLOPs without any additional training. Moreover, due to its differentiable design, one can also train a vision transformer equipped with ATS" (Abstract); "If a token is sampled more than once, we only keep one instance. As a consequence, the number of unique indices K ′ is often lower than K" (Sec. 3.2)

name: SPViT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; PiT-T/XS/S; Swin-T/S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.34 at 2.64 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); latency 60 ms vs 113 ms on a Samsung Galaxy S20
notes: Multi-head token selector (per-head MLP scores combined by a head-attention branch) with Gumbel-softmax; less informative tokens packed into one package token. A latency-sparsity look-up table of the target device sets per-block pruning rates through a latency-aware sparsity loss; per-image rates vary around the target. Layer-to-phase progressive training, selectors after layers 3/6/9; 60 epochs from pretrained weights. Latency on a Snapdragon 865 mobile CPU and a Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA (13.23 ms); no GPU throughput; batch size of the latency measurement not stated.
evidence: "We further introduce a soft pruning technique, which integrates the less informative tokens chosen by the selector module into a package token rather than discarding them completely" (Abstract); "we introduce the latency-aware sparsity loss to obtain the pruning rate of token constrained by the latency specifications of the target devices" (Sec. 4.3); "We follow most of the training settings as in DeiT and train all backbone models for 60 epochs" (Sec. 5)

name: SiT
main_result: LV-ViT-S (SiT-S): top-1 83.2 at 4.0 GFLOPs, 1892 img/s (baseline 83.3 at 6.6, 1360 img/s, V100)
notes: Token Slimming Module: X_hat = A X with A = softmax(W_q sigma(X W_k)^T / tau), a learned N_hat x N soft aggregation (keep ratio 0.5), inserted three times. Feature Recalibration Distillation: a reverse module reconstructs full tokens for block-wise distillation from the unslimmed teacher. Student initialized from the teacher weights and trained 125 epochs (300 with an extra CNN teacher). DeiT-S numbers from Table 1 (79.4 at 3308 img/s, +102.1% over the unreduced DeiT-S at 79.8 and 1637 img/s; the row at 79.8 and 2344 img/s is a second SiT variant). GFLOPs from Appendix Table 13 (keep ratio 0.5: 2.3 G, 3308 img/s, 2.0x). Throughput on a 16GB V100 (LeViT protocol).
evidence: "we first design a novel Token Slimming Module (TSM), which can boost the inference efficiency of ViTs by dynamic token aggregation" (Abstract); "our TSM softly integrates redundant tokens into fewer informative ones" (Abstract); "For initialization, we load all the weights from the corresponding teacher models to accelerate the convergence and train them for 125 epochs" (Sec. 4.1)

name: SaiT
main_result: DeiT-S (SaiT-S/M0.7 with DINO distillation): top-1 79.4 at 2.6 GFLOPs (baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Token importance = column sum of the attention matrix over heads and rows at one pruning layer (layer 3 for DeiT-S), one-stage pruning, no extra parameters. Mass-based selector keeps the smallest set whose scores sum to a threshold Mth (0.7 in training), adjustable at inference; value-based top-K variant also given. Dense/sparse alternate training so the same weights run unpruned at full accuracy. Optional DINO distillation for the token scores. 300 epochs from scratch. GFLOPs 2.6 is the average over the validation set (density 0.421). Throughput on a Quadro RTX 8000 with batch 64. No code URL.
evidence: "Instead of selecting a fixed number of tokens, we accumulate a varying number of the most important tokens up to a probability mass threshold" (Sec. 1); "We train SaiT-S and SaiT-LV from scratch with the proposed training framework for 300 epochs and 410 epochs, respectively" (Sec. 4.1)
